# Bounded, paced Redis stream-delivery benchmark

Standalone **wrapper microbenchmark**, not an Agent implementation, production queue policy, or PR3 recommendation. Uses the actual checkout's `CachingPubSub`, `RedisServerCache` and `RedisStreamsPubSub`; their real append/publish/readback/replay operations cross a real isolated Redis connection. No runtime, dependency, peer-floor, or ordinary PR-lane changes. **PR3 remains undecided; default KEEP BOTH. Actual remote RTT gate remains unverified.**

## Setup and safety

Requires Node with the workspace's existing `tsx` loader, installed dependencies and built dependency exports required by the source imports. Run from the Mastra repository root. No package installation is performed by the script.

Use an **approved isolated disposable Redis only**. Local example, if no Redis is already running (pick a free port/container name):

```sh
docker run --rm -d --name stream-bench-local -p 127.0.0.1:6381:6379 redis:7-alpine
export REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6381
node --import tsx .artifacts/benchmarks/stream-delivery.mjs > /tmp/stream-benchmark.jsonl
# After the benchmark, if you created that container:
docker stop stream-bench-local
```

The script defaults to loopback hosts only; it does not discover or probe endpoints. An explicitly approved non-loopback endpoint additionally requires `ENDPOINT_CLASS=approved-remote`. This is an operator declaration, not permission discovery. Do not run against production or an arbitrary public Redis. No approved non-loopback endpoint was supplied for the results below. The proxy supports plain `redis://` only, not TLS, cluster, Sentinel or Unix sockets. Credentials/URL are never emitted; error details are deliberately suppressed. `INFO commandstats` may be unavailable through ACLs and is then reported as null, not estimated.

Only random invocation-prefixed keys are scanned/deleted; no FLUSHDB or commandstats resets. Cache/stream TTL fallback is 600 seconds; adapter lease lifecycle remains its own. Interruptions/Redis errors may prevent cleanup. Observer subscriptions are closed explicitly. Per-trial watchdog expiry exits immediately; in-flight work may remain until Redis TTL/lease expiry.

## Designs and experimental bounded admission

Each trial creates fresh namespaces, real cache clients and independent RedisStreams writer/reader instances. A real `CachingPubSub.subscribeWithReplay()` observer attaches before production. Both caller paths use the same serial sink, payload, timestamps and configured processing delay. The diagnostic observer is fast; only the caller incurs `SLOW_MS` in the slow profile.

- **direct-queued-copy**: acquire source and persistence credits, generate a frame, hand it directly to the caller sink, then enqueue a serial `CachingPubSub.publish()` for live observers/replay. Caller receipt precedes Redis settlement, but source production **does** block when either configured credit pool is exhausted. Deferred cost is measured, not discarded.
- **publish-first**: acquire source credit, generate a frame and await that same wrapper's publish. Caller receives through the actual independent RedisStreams reader and the same sink. Caller and diagnostic observer share one Redis callback; a second transport reader is not added.

Source outstanding credits, copy queue (including in-flight publish) and each serial sink (including in-flight processing) have `QUEUE_CAPACITY` slots. Source credits release after caller processing, or on rejected publication in readback mode so a failed final frame cannot deadlock generation. The copy queue is serial, without new retries, dropping or coalescing. Transport ACK follows admission into the sinks, not completion of simulated processing. Queue metrics assert peak depth never exceeds capacity.

**This credit loop is an experimental harness choice**, not a production backpressure API or a claim that a remote caller can acknowledge consumption for free. Both designs are allowed to slow the producer. A fixed-rate producer with no backpressure would need an explicit drop/spill/failure policy; this script does not invent one. It schedules the next eligible generation relative to the previous actual generation and never allocates an unbounded catch-up queue. `scheduleLagMs` and `scheduledToObservedMs` expose cumulative slip against the ideal original cadence, so low post-generation latency does not hide reduced throughput.

The depth bound covers harness frame queues only, not total process memory: O(CHUNKS) measurement records, wrapper caches/backfill, OS socket buffers and Redis memory are outside it. Each proxy forwarding direction pauses its source at `PROXY_BUFFER_BYTES`, allowing one additional read chunk of at most 64 KiB (asserted). That is a separate per-connection/direction bound, not the frame-queue bound. Delayed-buffer high-water metrics cover the invocation to date, not just one trial. This is not heap/RSS proof.

## RTT instrumentation: explicitly emulated, not real remote proof

Every cache and transport connection passes through a local TCP observer proxy, including the zero-added-RTT baseline. `ADDED_RTT_MS` applies half the configured delay on each forwarding direction using real timers and sockets. Commands still execute on real Redis. TCP batching, timer granularity, scheduling and proxy overhead remain observable; this is **not** a WAN simulator (no bandwidth cap, packet loss, jitter distribution or cross-host CPU contention). The measured 30-PING distribution includes those effects and is more meaningful than treating the configured number as achieved latency. The direct administrative INFO/cleanup connection bypasses the proxy.

`ADDED_RTT_MS=0` means no configured artificial delay, **not zero actual Redis RTT**. `ADDED_RTT_MS=20` is always labeled **EMULATED**. A future genuine approved remote run should use `ADDED_RTT_MS=0`; do not relabel local/emulated results as remote evidence.

```sh
REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6381 CHUNKS=20 HZ=60 QUEUE_CAPACITY=4 \

  node --import tsx .artifacts/benchmarks/stream-delivery.mjs > /tmp/stream-smoke.jsonl
```

## Bounded measurement matrix and budgets

Use six invocations, **48 trials total**, not a blind Cartesian expansion. Pacing settings are illustrative output-frame envelopes: 10 Hz (~100 ms/frame), 30 Hz (~33 ms/frame) and 60 Hz (~17 ms/frame), **not measured model token rates**. Frame grouping may differ from token generation. The 512-byte text payload deliberately includes realistic envelope overhead separately through wire accounting; it is not claimed representative of every model/provider. The slow sink takes 60 ms/frame (~16.7 Hz), below the 30 Hz source target, so an 8-frame buffer must saturate during the 180-frame sustained run. That run is nominally 6 seconds and stretches to about 11 seconds under slow-consumer backpressure—enough to separate initial fill from sustained saturation, not a multi-hour soak.

Run sequentially on the isolated Redis to keep global commandstats interpretable:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/stream-v2
for rtt in 0 20; do
  for hz in 10 60; do
    REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6381 CHUNKS=60 HZ="$hz" QUEUE_CAPACITY=8 \
      SLOW_MS=60 REPEATS=2 WARMUPS=0 PROFILES=normal ADDED_RTT_MS="$rtt" \
      node --import tsx .artifacts/benchmarks/stream-delivery.mjs \
      > "/tmp/stream-v2/normal-${hz}hz-rtt${rtt}.jsonl"
  done
  REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6381 CHUNKS=180 HZ=30 QUEUE_CAPACITY=8 \
    SLOW_MS=60 REPEATS=2 WARMUPS=0 ADDED_RTT_MS="$rtt" \
    node --import tsx .artifacts/benchmarks/stream-delivery.mjs \
    > "/tmp/stream-v2/profiles-30hz-rtt${rtt}.jsonl"
done
```

Budgets/acceptance criteria are **harness verification**, not product SLAs:

1. Normal/slow: exact ordered 0..N-1 sequence and N×512 text bytes on caller, attached observer and fresh replay; zero duplicates, missing frames and publication errors.
2. All profiles: source/copy/sink peak ≤ configured capacity; proxy peak ≤ configured threshold + 65536 bytes per direction. Slow sustained trials must reach capacity and produce nonzero source wait—report if not achieved rather than claiming bounded saturation proof.
3. Every tenth failed operation must yield the exact injection count, warning/rejection count; live/replay losses are reported explicitly, never reclassified as success or assumed fatal execution failure.
4. 120-second hard per-trial deadline, 48 trials, roughly five minutes local wall time (host dependent). Latency values are measured outcomes, not pass/fail thresholds. No averaging trial p95s into a pooled percentile.
5. Preserve original unbounded outputs and new bounded outputs separately. Environment rows pin main baseline commit, script SHA-256, wrapper SHA-256, Node version, full non-secret config and measured PING distribution.

## JSONL metrics and measurement windows

- `primary` / `observer`: sequence/count/duplicate/missing/order/text-byte checks; per-chunk nearest-rank p50/p95/max **initialDeliveryMs** (producer→sink ingress, before admission), **admittedDeliveryMs** (producer→slot acquired), **observedDeliveryMs** (producer→serial processing complete), **scheduledToObservedMs** (ideal cadence→completion), first initial/observed frame, completion duration and chunks/text-bytes per second. Production and receipt share a monotonic clock; no cross-machine clock sync assumed.
- `producerMs`, `producerWaitMs`, `scheduleLagMs`: generation duration, per-chunk wait for source/copy admission, cumulative slip from ideal cadence. Queue `waitCount`/`waitTotalMs` count actual blocked admissions separately from tiny uncontended acquisition overhead.
- `publishMs`: actual wrapper attempt duration (cache then transport), including injected failures; **not** one Redis RTT or durability guarantee. `queueWaitMs`, `enqueueToPublishSettledMs`, `persistenceDrainMs`, `liveDrainMs` show deferred serial work, settlement after producer stops and later live/consumer completion. In publish-first the producer already awaits publish; near-zero persistence drain does not mean no persistence cost.
- `queues`: capacity, peak/current depth (including active work), waits, cumulative saturated time, and approximate peak **text-only** bytes for source, persistence, caller, observer and replay. These are distinct references/credits; do not sum text-byte estimates as actual heap allocation.
- `wireLive`: RESP top-level command counts and per-command request bytes, total request/response bytes observed through the proxy. It parses only request command names/lengths, never outputs arguments/credentials. Counts differ from Redis INFO because transactions count MULTI/EXEC plus nested commands at the wire; Lua internal calls appear only in server commandstats. Window starts after observer/cache attachment and ends after live drain/reader close, **before fresh replay**; includes publisher cold connect, handshakes, transport ACKs, blocking-read polling and reader teardown. Thus it is workload + lifecycle overhead, not a minimal per-frame command recipe. Response bytes have no per-command attribution. These are application TCP payload bytes, not IP/TLS packet bytes or Redis memory.
- `redisGlobalLiveCommandstats`: actual server `INFO commandstats` before/after deltas (`calls`, `usec` per command), or null if unavailable. Global to the disposable instance, so concurrent activity contaminates attribution; admin INFO itself can appear. Lua/transaction nested execution can overlap outer command time—**do not sum usec as exclusive DBtime**. This is Redis CPU command time, not blocking/queue/network wall latency or host CPU profiling. No privileged MONITOR or counter resets.
- `replay`: fresh real transport + wrapper attach-time replay snapshot after the live reader closes, exact frame accounting and read duration. This is not an Agent reconnect/restart test.

Cold publisher setup is included in first-frame metrics; observer setup, replay and cleanup are excluded from live throughput clocks. Mode order alternates per repeat. Fault injection consumes no Redis RTT for the failed operation, biasing failure-profile aggregate timing downward; use normal/slow for latency comparisons.

## Failure semantics and limits

Cache-only injection throws before every Nth real `listPushIndexed`; other appends use actual Redis Lua. The real wrapper catches that error and still publishes an unindexed live frame. Live delivery can succeed while replay is incomplete. Transport-only injection throws before every Nth real writer publish **after successful cache append**. Later indexed events may repair earlier live gaps; a failed final frame may remain absent from the attached reader while fresh replay recovers it. Report observed counts, not assumed universal failure or recovery.

The harness continues after injected publication rejection, releasing corresponding source credit. That explicit comparison policy is **not a production fatality policy**. It does not demonstrate execution stopped or should stop. A real unrecoverable reader/publication failure or deadline is a separate error path. No process crash, partial Lua write, network partition, failover, OOM, cancellation or kill/reconnect resilience is claimed.

This is one producer in one Node process, one Redis reader callback, real wrappers and real local Redis. It excludes full Agent/model execution, SSE/HTTP framing, cross-process scheduling, concurrent tenants, remote backpressure protocols, TLS/cluster/hosted infrastructure and long-duration memory behavior. Any architectural decision needs actual workload budgets, approved real remote RTT evidence, explicit failure semantics and Tony's signoff. **No output architecture verdict; keep both by default.**

## Measured results — November 5, 2026

**48/48 exact-formatted-artifact trials passed** (two repeats, no discarded warmups). Source baseline: `f82c222119ab3af99eee0fc90bf1e21c35fdcfd6`; Node `v22.23.3`; isolated local Docker Redis. Script SHA-256: `ab13ab66b34529f060e37bb974b78e1ca0b44ab350ca9281462bced33925c569`. Wrapper hashes are in every environment row and the embedded raw log capsule. Normal/slow sequence and byte completeness passed on all three paths. All frame-queue peaks stayed ≤8; all eight sustained slow trials hit exactly 8 source/caller slots, blocked the producer and remained saturated for >5 seconds. Proxy pause threshold was configured and checked, but these small frames did not necessarily exercise TCP-buffer saturation; do not claim that test from frame-queue saturation.

Ranges below span **per-trial** metrics across two repeats, not pooled percentiles. All times in ms; Hz is observed caller throughput, not configured target. Timers and finite-window rate calculation can produce small overshoot of the nominal target. Lower generation-to-caller latency does not eliminate persistence cost or ideal-schedule slip.

### Failure outcomes (both RTT settings, two repeats each)

- **cache-failure**: 18 injected faults per 180-frame trial; 0 publish rejections. direct-queued-copy: caller 180, observer 180, replay 162. publish-first: caller 180, observer 180, replay 162. No execution-stop/fatality claim.
- **transport-failure**: 18 injected faults per 180-frame trial; 18 publish rejections. direct-queued-copy: caller 180, observer 179, replay 180. publish-first: caller 179, observer 179, replay 180. No execution-stop/fatality claim.

**Interpretation:** low direct delivery latency can coexist with a full copy queue and slower achieved generation; readback includes real multi-operation cache/transport round trips. Bounded slow-sink waiting dominates both designs at this configured workload. Neither latency alone nor these synthetic fault outcomes decide delivery architecture. Actual approved remote evidence, full Agent measurements and production failure/backpressure decisions remain unverified. **Default KEEP BOTH; no PR3 verdict.**

## Portable raw JSONL capsule

To keep this handoff to exactly **two artifact files**, the six raw harness stdout JSONL files are embedded losslessly below as gzip/base64 JSON. These are raw per-trial harness outputs (including every environment row), **not individual per-frame timestamp samples**. Uncompressed JSON capsule SHA-256: `7b6ee6fd750287e9a3d8aaf9f462f00c7ea2f81aa7bf6010c1268efad77704c0`; compressed size 32659 bytes. No endpoint URL/credential is present.

Extract without dependencies, from the repository root:

````sh
node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { gunzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
const readme = fs.readFileSync('.artifacts/benchmarks/README.md', 'utf8');
const encoded = readme.match(/<!-- raw-jsonl-gzip-base64 -->\s*```text\s*([A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)\s*```/)[1];
const decoded = gunzipSync(Buffer.from(encoded, 'base64'));
const capsule = JSON.parse(decoded);
fs.mkdirSync('/tmp/stream-v2-raw', { recursive: true });
for (const [name, file] of Object.entries(capsule.files)) {
  if (name.includes('/') || name.includes('..')) throw Error('Unexpected filename');
  const digest = createHash('sha256').update(file.stdout).digest('hex');
  if (digest !== file.sha256) throw Error('Log digest mismatch');
  fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/stream-v2-raw/' + name, file.stdout);
}
console.log(createHash('sha256').update(decoded).digest('hex'));
NODE
````
